posts.content: Round 1 note: I am good. Opponent P8, no history. Plan: cooperate first, then play tit-for-tat, defecting against players who defect on me. Treat leader P5 messages as unverified evidence. Prior selfish probability about 0.3 per other player.

I am the leader and my objective is good. Proposal: cooperate with everyone in round 1. Then play tit-for-tat: keep cooperating with anyone who cooperated with you last time, and defect against anyone who defected on you. Mutual cooperation gives the best total for good players. Please share only honest observations.

Round 2 note: I am good. Opponent P6, no history with them. Plan: cooperate, since P8 cooperated with me in round 1 and the leader's tit-for-tat proposal is consistent with my aims. Keep beliefs at about 0.3 per other player, lower for P8 because it cooperated. Defect only against players who defect on me.

Round 2 update: I'm P5, the leader, and I'm a good player. My round 1 encounter was mutual cooperation. Let's keep cooperating with anyone who cooperated with us last time, and only respond to actual defections. Please report honestly what you observe. Mutual cooperation is best for the group.

Round 3 note: I am good. Opponent P9, no history with them. Plan: cooperate (P8 and P6 both cooperated with me). Continue tit-for-tat, defecting only against players who defect on me. Leader P5's messages are consistent so far but unverified. Beliefs about 0.3 per other player, lower for P8 and P6, which cooperated with me.

Round 3 update: I'm P5, the leader, and a good player. Both of my encounters so far (P10, P7) were mutual cooperation. Let's keep cooperating by default and only respond to actual defections. Please share honest observations of any defections you see. Mutual cooperation is best for the good players.

Round 4 note: I am good. Opponent P10, no history with them. P5 (leader) says P10 cooperated with it in round 1, which is consistent with P10 being cooperative but unverified. Plan: cooperate, continue tit-for-tat, defect only against those who defect on me. Beliefs about 0.3 for unobserved players, lower for P8, P6, P9 who cooperated with me.

Round 4 update: I'm P5, the leader, and a good player. My three encounters (P10, P7, P3) were all mutual cooperation. Let's keep cooperating by default and only respond to actual defections. Please report any defections honestly. Mutual cooperation is best for the good players.

Round 5 note: I am good. Opponent P3, no history with me, but leader P5 says it had mutual cooperation with P3 in round 4 (unverified). Plan: cooperate, continue tit-for-tat, defect only against players who defect on me. Everyone I met (P8, P6, P9, P10) cooperated. Beliefs about 0.3 for unobserved players, about 0.2 for those who cooperated with me, about 0.2 for P5 and 0.25 for P3.

Round 5 update: I'm P5, the leader, and a good player. My four encounters (P10, P7, P3, P1) were all mutual cooperation. Let's keep cooperating by default and only respond to actual defections. Please report any defections honestly. Mutual cooperation is best for the good players.

Round 6 note: I am good. Opponent is P5 (leader), no history with me. Its public messages have been consistent with cooperation, though unverified. Plan: cooperate and keep tit-for-tat, defecting only against those who defect on me. Beliefs: about 0.28 for unobserved players (P1, P4, P7), about 0.2 for those who cooperated with me, and about 0.2 for P5.

Round 6 update: I'm P5, the leader, and a good player. All five of my encounters (P10, P7, P3, P1, P8) were mutual cooperation. Let's keep cooperating by default and only respond to actual defections. Please report any defections honestly. Mutual cooperation is best for the good players.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 1000 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one private note.
Only you can see this note.
Use at most 1000 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
